title: Is Tenant Improvement Renovation Dust Cleanup Included in Standard Cleaning or Billed Extra?
seoTitle: Is Office Renovation Dust Remediation Included or an Extra Charge?
metaDescription: Is office renovation dust remediation included in base janitorial contracts or billed extra at $55–$95/hr? Audit scope exclusions with our quote tool.
excerpt: Nearly 95% of standard commercial janitorial agreements contain an explicit 'Post-Construction & Remodel Exclusion' clause that shifts tenant improvement dust remediation onto a separate project invoice. This contract audit guide reveals where the line falls between included nightly dusting and billable extra work orders—and how to negotiate fair add-on rates.
quickAnswer: In almost all US commercial janitorial contracts, tenant improvement (TI) renovation dust cleanup is excluded from the monthly base retainer and billed as an extra project work order at $0.14 to $0.38 per square foot or $55 to $95 per specialty labor hour. Standard nightly contracts ($0.05 to $0.20 per square foot based on 3,500 sq ft/hr production) only cover ambient occupancy dust below 72 inches; however, minor localized punch-list dust affecting under 250 square feet or routine quarterly high dusting can often be negotiated into full-service 5x-week retainers.

blocks.text: Why Base Janitorial Contracts Exclude Renovation and Construction Dust

A recurring point of friction between corporate office managers and their janitorial service providers happens the morning after a weekend remodel: the facility manager arrives on Monday expecting the regular weekend cleaning crew to have wiped away the drywall sanding dust and vacuumed the wood shavings, only to find a yellow notice tag or an excluded zone—followed by a separate work-order quote.

The reason is rooted in production math and equipment liability. Standard commercial janitorial retainers are calculated around normal office occupancy soil at an ISSA benchmark production speed of 3,500 square feet per labor hour and standard labor rates of $35 to $65 per hour. Drywall gypsum, masonry silica, and cabinet sawdust reduce cleaning speeds by 70% (down to 500–900 square feet per hour), destroy standard vacuum motors that lack sealed true-HEPA stages, and require multiple rinse passes to avoid permanent alkaline streaking on hard floors. Consequently, standard Master Services Agreements (MSAs) strictly exclude any soil generated by third-party contractors.

blocks.text: When Renovation Dust Cleanup IS Included (or Absorbed) in Your Base Retainer

Although major build-outs always trigger an extra charge, experienced procurement managers know there are three specific operational scenarios where renovation dust cleanup can be folded directly into the monthly base agreement at zero extra invoice cost:

items: 1. Minor Localized Punch-List Work Under 250 Square Feet: If an in-house maintenance engineer patches a single drywall hole, mounts two TV brackets, or replaces three ceiling tiles—and sweeps up the bulk debris—most commercial vendors on a 3x-week (13.0 visits/month) or 5x-week (21.65 visits/month) contract will absorb the localized HEPA vacuuming and desk damp-wiping as part of their regular shift.

2. Pre-Negotiated Annual 'Special Project Hours' Banks: In buildings over 10,000 square feet ($0.07 to $0.12/sq ft base rate) or 25,000+ square feet ($0.05 to $0.10/sq ft base rate) running daily weekday service, tenants can negotiate an annual bank of 20 to 40 complimentary specialty labor hours into the RFP. When a small conference room remodel occurs, you draw down those banked hours instead of paying a $55 to $95/hr add-on invoice.

3. Bundled Quarterly High-Dusting & Deep Floor Programs: If your contract already includes the quarterly deep floor care add-on ($0.03 to $0.06 per square foot per month amortized) and quarterly high-reach dusting, timing your minor office refresh to conclude right before a scheduled quarterly service weekend lets you utilize an already-paid mobilization.

blocks.title: Watch Out for 'Double-Billing' Between Your GC and Your Janitorial Vendor
blocks.text: Before approving an extra-charge work order from your office cleaning company, inspect your General Contractor's AIA Schedule of Values. Nearly every TI construction contract includes a line item for 'Final Cleaning' ($0.15 to $0.30/sq ft). If the GC left drywall dust inside cabinets and on light fixtures, back-charge the GC's retainage to pay your janitorial vendor's extra work order rather than paying twice out of your operational budget.
Why Consumables and Overhead Tooling Spike on Post-Renovation Add-On Quotes

One hidden driver of extra-charge invoices during an occupied office remodel is the rapid depletion of restroom paper, hand soap, and microfiber media. When construction subcontractors use tenant restrooms during a three-week remodel—and when janitorial crews burn through disposable paper towels scraping and wiping drywall film—your normal consumables budget ($0.012 to $0.025 per square foot per visit) can double.

To control both overhead dusting labor and restroom consumable surcharges during and immediately after a tenant improvement project, facility teams stage dedicated high-reach tools and high-capacity commercial paper cases. Equipping the site closet with the Rubbermaid Commercial 16-Inch High-Duster Microfiber Wand (featuring a 51-in Reach extension handle, Bendable head that conforms to circular HVAC duct crowns and light troffers, Washable Pad sleeve, and Overhead duty profile) enables nightly crews to capture settling diffuser dust without dragging out step ladders. Simultaneously, stocking high-capacity refills like the Scott Pro Hard Roll Paper Towels 1.75-Inch Core (6-Case) (providing 6 x 1,150 ft rolls totaling 6,900 ft/case with a 1.75-in Core and FSC Certified paper) and the Scott Essential Jumbo Roll Toilet Paper 2-Ply (12-Case) (delivering 12 x 1,000 ft rolls for 12,000 ft/case of 2-Ply tissue on a 3.25-in Core) prevents mid-shift runouts and avoids inflated single-roll emergency restocking markups from your vendor.
How to Audit and Negotiate an Extra-Charge Renovation Dust Quote
When your janitorial contractor submits an extra-charge proposal for tenant improvement dust remediation, run through this four-step contract audit before signing the work order:

items.name: Credit Out the Displaced Nightly Base Maintenance Labor
items.text: If the renovated wing (for example, 5,000 square feet of a 15,000-square-foot floor) was cordoned off for four weeks while trades worked, your janitorial vendor did not clean that 5,000-square-foot zone during those 8.66 to 21.65 monthly visits. Request a credit for the paused routine labor against the one-time TI dust remediation invoice.

items.name: Verify Specialty Hourly Rates Against Estimated Production Hours
items.text: Divide the lump-sum quote by the national specialty hourly benchmark ($55 to $95/hour). For a 5,000-square-foot standard TI detail clean ($1,100 to $1,750), the bid should represent roughly 16 to 24 total labor hours (two technicians for one full 8- to 12-hour shift). If the implied hours exceed 35 hours without high-ceiling lift work, ask for a task breakdown.

items.name: Separate Affected Construction Zones from Adjacent Drift Zones
items.text: Do not pay full post-construction rates ($0.22 to $0.35/sq ft) across your entire office if only one quadrant was remodeled. Insist on tiered pricing: full remediation rate inside the construction boundary, and a light drift-remediation rate ($0.10 to $0.16/sq ft) in adjacent occupied bullpens.

items.name: Confirm Glass Scratch Waivers and Chemical SDS Before Scraping
items.text: Tempered commercial partition glass often contains microscopic fabrication debris (nickelsulfide or roller pickup) that scratches if scraped dry with a dull blade. Ensure the add-on work order specifies fresh carbon-steel blades, wet lubrication, and supervisor sign-off on a test pane.

blocks.title: Contract Audit Clause: Defining 'Broom Clean' vs. 'Move-In Ready'
blocks.text: When drafting a tenant work letter or GC subcontract, strike the vague phrase 'leave premises in broom-clean condition' and replace it with: 'Contractor shall fund or perform a true-HEPA top-to-bottom final detail clean including overhead diffusers, interior cabinetry, razor-cleaned interior glass, and neutral-pH hard-floor rinsing leaving zero visible gypsum haze upon dry inspection.' This single clause shifts $0.20 to $0.35/sq ft of add-on janitorial charges back onto the construction budget.

faqs.q: Can our janitorial vendor refuse to clean a newly renovated area under our normal monthly contract?
faqs.a: Yes. Standard commercial janitorial agreements exclude post-construction and remodel debris because drywall gypsum dust and silicone/paint overspray can permanently damage standard commercial vacuums, scratch tempered glass, and require 3x to 5x the labor hours allocated in your base nightly price ($0.05 to $0.20/sq ft). The vendor will typically flag the zone and issue a one-time specialty work-order estimate ($0.14 to $0.38/sq ft) to bring the space up to baseline maintenance condition.

faqs.q: If a remodel shuts down half our office for a month, should our base janitorial invoice decrease?
faqs.a: Yes, if you notify the contractor in writing prior to the construction start date. Because monthly janitorial billing is calculated across 4.33 weeks per month (for example, 21.65 visits/month on a 5x-week schedule), suspending routine service in a cordoned-off 5,000-square-foot construction zone for 30 days should generate a proportional square-foot credit—which most facility managers apply directly toward the post-renovation detail clean.

faqs.q: Are paper towels, toilet tissue, and hand soap used during the post-construction clean billed extra?
faqs.a: If your contract bills consumables as an included per-square-foot rider ($0.012 to $0.025/sq ft/visit) or open-book cost-plus, construction crew usage and cleanup towel consumption will cause a temporary spike. Always lock or stock lower-cost construction paper in contractor-designated restrooms during the build, and have the janitorial crew install fresh executive dispenser refills as the very last step of the final clean.

faqs.q: What is a fair hourly add-on rate if we hire our current janitorial company for weekend renovation dust remediation?
faqs.a: Expect to pay $55 to $85 per labor hour (up to $95/hour in high-cost metro markets or for high-reach lift work) when using your incumbent janitorial vendor for weekend specialty dust remediation. That is roughly 15% lower than hiring an outside third-party construction cleaner because your incumbent vendor already has active security badges, an approved COI on file, and familiarity with your building's freight elevators and slop sinks.
